paper_title: AI4Reading: Chinese Audiobook Interpretation System Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary:
AI4Reading: Chinese Audiobook Interpretation System Based on Multi-Agent Collaboration - Minjiang Huang, Jipeng Qiang, Yi Zhu, Chaowei Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao, Kui Yu, 2025

The system targets automatic generation of Chinese audiobook interpretation content, a production setting where raw book material must be transformed into a podcast-like spoken script that preserves source semantics while improving accessibility and discourse coherence. The technical objective is explicitly tripartite: maintain accurate content preservation, increase comprehensibility for listeners, and impose a logical narrative structure suitable for long-form audio delivery. AI4Reading operationalizes this as a multi-agent LLM pipeline coupled with speech synthesis, rather than a single-pass generation model. The architecture contains 11 specialized agents with role separation across topic analysis, case analysis, editing, narration, and proofreading; these agents collaboratively identify major themes, retrieve or formulate real-world cases, reorganize content into a listener-oriented progression, and rewrite text into natural spoken Chinese. The built artifact is an end-to-end audiobook-interpretation system that produces both interpretative scripts and synthesized speech, and the paper was released as an ACL 2025 system demonstration with public code and a demo video. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23300?utm_source=openai))

The reported evaluation compares AI4Reading outputs against expert-produced interpretations rather than only intrinsic generation metrics, indicating that the main benchmark is practical quality in a human-authored reference setting. The central empirical claim is asymmetric: speech generation quality still lags expert production, but the generated interpretation scripts are judged simpler and more accurate than expert counterparts, suggesting the multi-agent decomposition improves factual faithfulness and readability at the script level even when downstream TTS expressiveness remains a bottleneck. Publicly accessible metadata for the paper does not expose detailed quantitative tables, exact dataset sizes, or metric values in the abstract-level sources available via search, so no reliable numeric gains beyond that qualitative comparison can be stated without fabricating unsupported results. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.23300?utm_source=openai))
